elements.problem: Header sets the precondition (patient with constipation). Encoded as the Constipation finding in the priority rule.
evidence: Urgent: constipation with no stools or flatus for 24 hours :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Constipation" "finding"))

elements.problem: Parts: (a) no stools, (b) no flatus, (c) abdominal pain/distension. (c) is encoded correctly as an or of Abdominal pain and Distension of abdomen. (a) and (b) are encoded as (>= (onset X) (time_ago 24 hours)). That means the onset was within the last 24 hours. The page means none for at least the past 24 hours, so a patient obstipated for 3 days would fail the rule. The direction or semantics of the time comparison is likely wrong (should be onset at or before 24 hours ago, or a duration >= 24 h). 'No stools' is mapped to the Obstipation disorder, which means absolute constipation rather than simply 'no stools'. Acceptable but loose. The check task for this box also lists Bed-ridden, Seen by palliative care service and Chronic constipation with overflow, which belong to the impaction bullet, not this box.
evidence: Urgent: constipation with no stools or flatus for 24 hours :: (>= (onset (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Obstipation" "disorder"))) (time_ago 24 hours))
Urgent: constipation with no stools or flatus for 24 hours :: (>= (onset (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Unable to break wind" "finding"))) (time_ago 24 hours))

Check for urgent constipation conditions :: (check_for (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Obstipation" "disorder")) ... (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Distension of abdomen" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Bed-ridden" "finding")) ...)

elements.problem: Refer same day is encoded as priority Urgent. This is a reasonable mapping to the priority level.
evidence: Urgent: constipation with no stools or flatus for 24 hours :: Urgent

elements.scope_reason: Contains the impaction likely logic (and anaemia likely, not representable). Other bullets are management or cross-references.
parts_missing: Age > 65 years is one of the or-triggers for checking for impaction, and it is not encoded in the task or in the diagnosis rule
Anaemia likely if Hb < 12 (woman) or < 13 (man): not_representable (lab value, no unit), correctly absent
Check TSH if weakness/tiredness, weight gain, low mood, dry skin or cold intolerance: management step, absent by design
elements.problem: Impaction rule triggers only on Bed-ridden, Seen by palliative care service and Chronic constipation with overflow. The age > 65 trigger is missing from both the task and the probable rule. Rectal solid immobile stool is mapped to Hard stool with finding site Rectum structure. This is acceptable, but it is the only finding site check and needs to be resolvable. 'Impaction likely' is encoded as probable, correct.
evidence: Diagnose probable faecal impaction in constipation :: (and (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Constipation" "finding")) (or (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Bed-ridden" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Seen by palliative care service" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Chronic constipation with overflow" "disorder"))) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Hard stool" "finding") (finding_site (snomed_concept "Rectum structure" "body structure"))))
Check for faecal impaction in constipation :: (check_for (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Hard stool" ...)))

elements.scope_reason: The page does not say 'consider cancer'. It says if symptoms, discuss/refer, with risk factors listed. A possible cancer diagnosis is a reasonable but not explicit reading.
parts_missing: Increased risk: age > 50 and any of previous colorectal cancer, polyps, ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, family history of colorectal cancer in first-degree relative, multiple polyps or Lynch syndrome
elements.problem: Symptom list is encoded (diarrhoea, rectal bleeding, haematochezia, abdominal discomfort, colic, flatulence, tenesmus, weight loss, asthenia, fatigue). The risk-factor branch (age > 50 plus history) is entirely absent. The possible rule fires on any single symptom with constipation and ignores age. Abdominal pain is in the possible rule but not in the check task, and Flatulence symptom and Abdominal colic are loose stand-ins for 'gas' and 'cramps'.
evidence: Diagnose possible colorectal cancer in constipation :: (and (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Constipation" "finding")) (or ... (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Tenesmus of anus and/or rectum" "finding")) ...))
Check for colorectal cancer symptoms in constipation :: (check_for (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Diarrhea" "finding")) ...)

elements.problem: Treatment doses and referral steps (laxatives, rehabilitation referral, refer if no response) are management, out of scope by design. The referral criteria (age > 65/frail, postpartum, spinal disease, etc.) carry no diagnosis.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: constipation with no stools or flatus for 24 hours
rule_level_problems.problem: (>= (onset X) (time_ago 24 hours)) most likely means onset within the last 24 hours, the opposite of no stools for at least 24 hours. Patients obstipated for longer than 24 hours would not be triaged Urgent.

check_for mixes the red-box urgent items with Bed-ridden, Seen by palliative care service and Chronic constipation with overflow, which belong to the impaction bullet and are not used by the urgent priority rule. The Flatus finding is checked, but the task triggers on Constipation only.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose possible colorectal cancer in constipation
rule_level_problems.problem: Ignores the age > 50 and risk-factor conditions. Fires for any age adult with any single common symptom, so it over-triggers. Abdominal pain is in the rule but not in the matching check task.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable faecal impaction in constipation
rule_level_problems.problem: Age > 65 trigger from the page is missing.

summary: The most consequential problem is the urgent priority rule: the 24-hour comparisons on onset are most likely inverted (onset within 24 hours rather than for at least 24 hours), so true obstipation would be missed. The urgent check task also mixes in impaction items. The colorectal cancer and impaction rules lose the age and risk-factor conditions (> 50 with history; > 65).
